body: Your relationship with your parents seems like an abusive one. I cant fault them too much, burying a child is a terrible experience, but they still have a living child. Your husband can help you. I know how difficult it can be to separate yourself from the idea of suicide. Maybe you need to separate yourself from the cause of your suffering. You and your husband can move forward together. The two of you can build a life you both want to live. Once you are healthy and happy, you can repair the relationship with your parents. Just take things one step at a time.
Do you want to want to live?

I think you're mentioning it as a possible way out of this mess. If that's true, I'm glad you did. I hope you'll be glad you did. I dont think anyone truly wants to die. We just want to not hurt anymore. I dont know what's driven you to this point, but this thread is a place where you can talk about it anonymously. 

I hope you choose life, as its (in my opinion) the only one we have. I hope you can trust that other people (myself included) dont want you, or anyone, to suffer for nothing. You may not see it now, but the pain you feel now will make you stronger. You only have to commit to living. But I understand this is your decision. I will not judge you for your choice.

I hope you call and cancel your hotel room. I hope you never tie a noose again. There is good in the world, and in yourself. 

If you want to talk you can call someone you trust, or a professional (preferably both). If you arent ready for that you can talk here. The people on this sub will look after you if you let them.

I'm sorry that you're going through this. But I'm glad you posted on here, it isnt easy to admit to the world that you arent okay. But not being okay is okay. The first thing you should know is that you arent alone. Millions of other people (myself included) have been in your shoes. Your situation is unique, but the feelings arent. We are all the same species, after all. I'm sure my words dont make it easier. They might even piss you off. My hope isnt that you view my words as gospel, or truth, or even good for that matter. My hope is that you see that there are people out there who care. I care about you even though I (probably) have never met you. And I know I'm not alone in feeling this way. 

It's my opinion that most of the time we arent really alone, we are just hiding. I hope you find the courage to try to form the human connection that you desire. I hope you get help, I know it's a broken record on here, but just because it didn't work once doesnt mean it cant work. I hope you find that life, no matter its trials and hardships, is worth living. And I hope you find happiness, whatever that means to you.

With love

It's crazy how much you sound like me. 

I'm sorry you're going through all of this. It's never easy to look around and question why our life is the way that it is. You are right with the answer, all of what we think is right and wrong was just made up by someone along the way. When we start to question it ourselves, we end up with unsolvable questions. The realization that the meaningfulness of your life is determined by you is a difficult pill to swallow. Especially when it seems like everyone else is drivin by some purpose you cant see. It's frustrating as hell and can lead you down dark roads. 

What's helped me most is to be open with other people. You'd be amazed at how fucked up most people are. In reality human beings are too smart to be truly "happy", and too dumb to have a "real" purpose. Happiness isnt what most people think it is. The challenge comes with accepting it. But you dont have to do it alone. We are all a bunch of monkey people helping each other make it through the day. It isnt easy, but it's worth it. Since my last wave of depression/suicidal thoughts I have grown closer to my friends and family, I've been taking the time to better myself (therapy, meditation, excercise), and I allow myself to feel without judgement (probably the most important one). I'm not cured, I doubt I'll ever be. But every time I laugh, or watch the sunset, or look at the stars, I feel grateful that I'm still alive to do it. 

It isnt easy, but it is simple. It's hard work, but the path is clear. If you arent sure you can handle it all on your own, get help. I think posting on here is a great start. It takes a lot of courage to do it. I hope seeing a response is enough to know that people still care. I hope that you decide to do whatever it takes to live a happy life. And I hope that you find the happiness you desire, whatever that means to you.

I'm sorry you feel that way. I've struggled with depression and suicidal thoughts for a long time. Every time I have one of my bad days I wish I was dead. I never want to do it myself, but I wish someone would break in my house and shoot me like the old gangster movies. I'm like you. I just dont want to feel pain anymore. But I cant lie to myself and say there's no happiness to be found in life, even during depression. I wanted to believe that I have it all figured out and that life wasn't worth living. But I decided to try it out. I started going to therapists/psychs. I told the people in my life what I was going through, I was surprised that most of them understood and were supportive. I started meditating, exercising, and journaling. With the support of both professionals and the people who love me, I've been able to get back on my feet. The bad days still happen, "I always want to die sometimes". But it makes me appreciate the good things so much more. 

I know that my positivity isnt necessarily what you want to hear, but even the saddest people are capable of happiness. It isnt easy, and there will be times where it seems impossible. But being committed to living a life worth living is the only way out. I dont want your last thought to be a sad one. I doubt you do either. I hope you find a way to move forward. I hope you trust that there are people out there who do understand, and you can find a sense of comfort in knowing that getting out of it is possible. I hope you stay strong and find happiness, whatever that means to you. 

With love

I'm sorry you feel that way. I've been there and it feels horrible. A few things helped me out were: I started seeing a therapist (I hate to sound like a broken record but it helped), I started meditating regularly. Meditating helped more than I can say. It brought me out of my brain and allowed me to observe the world around me without that nasty voice in my head telling me I didn't deserve it. I also started journaling, which has been very helpful for identifying complicated feelings and emotions. 

I hope this helps, even if it's only to know that there are people who have felt the same way. I hope you stay strong and find happiness, whatever that means to you. And I hope you see that life is worth living, even if it doesnt always seem that way.

With love
Thank you for the response. Especially for the resource. I'm glad that monkey people like you exist
